title: Third QA speed improvement
scope: Prepared-command wall time for the same 24-case fixture (12 behaviors at 1440x900 and 390x844) with six seeded defect groups; every run audited with the verbatim v2 audit. Excludes agent reading/authoring, dependency installs and fixture server startup.

webmcp_vs_ui_setup_adjacent_pairs.note: Cyclic rotation keeps e2e_v3 immediately before webmcp_v3 in every round.

final_pass.protocol: 1 excluded warm-up round + 5 measured rounds, mode order rotated by round, sequential, 8s untimed cool-down before each command

manifest.sampling: one excluded warm-up round, then 5 measured rounds with mode order rotated by round; sequential, one command at a time

pass 1.note: No cool-down. Outside load in rounds 3-4 raised CPU-seconds per run about 30% for parallel modes.

pass 2.note: No cool-down, started about one minute after pass 1. CPU-seconds per run about 30% higher throughout; 1-minute load reached 17.8.

tuning.note: Pilot A/B medians from interleaved runs on the same machine and fixture, each run audited with the verbatim v2 audit (all runs qualified). Directional evidence for choosing the shipped design; the final claim is comparison/summary.json. For four-round pilots, "median" is the true median where per-run times were kept and "upper_median" (the higher middle value) otherwise.

pilots.note: Only summaries were kept: upper_median is the higher middle wall time; pre_run and runner_span are true medians.

cpu_breakdown_one_run.note: Sampled per-process CPU seconds during one early-start run (headless shell, one shared browser); short-lived processes are undercounted.

rejected: Uncapped frame rate: slower and more CPU.
More files/workers than 2 files x 4 workers: no faster on this 8-core machine.
Playwright-managed launch (launchPersistentContext with a debugging port): keeps a second CDP client attached to every browser.
In-process e2e runner API: about 60-85ms less boot, but the shipped launcher would lose the e2e CLI interface.
